stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \ln\left| x - 2 \right| + \frac{\left(x^{2} - x - 12\right)\left(x^{2} - 11 x + 30\right)}{\left(x^{2} - 3 x - 18\right)\left(x - 5\right)} \). The graph of \( f \) has exactly one vertical asymptote, the line \( x = c \). Find the value of \( c \).

worked_solution.text: The rational part has numerator \( \left(x - 6\right) \left(x - 5\right) \left(x - 4\right) \left(x + 3\right) \) and denominator \( \left(x - 6\right) \left(x - 5\right) \left(x + 3\right) \).

The factors at \( x = -3 \), \( x = 5 \), and \( x = 6 \) divide out, so away from those inputs the rational part equals \( x - 4 \), a polynomial. Those three inputs are removable discontinuities, not asymptotes.
The only input left where \( f \) is undefined is \( x = 2 \), where \( \ln\left| x - 2 \right| \) is undefined.
As \( x \to 2 \) from either side, \( \left| x - 2 \right| \to 0^+ \), so the logarithm decreases without bound while the polynomial part stays finite: \( f(x) \to -\infty \) on both sides.
So the line \( x = 2 \) is the only vertical asymptote, and \( c = 2 \).
